question.prompt:
In rectangle \(ADEH,\) points \(B\) and \(C\) trisect \(\overline{AD},\) and points \(G\) and \(F\) trisect \(\overline{HE}.\) In addition, \(AH = AC = 2.\) What is the area of quadrilateral \(WXYZ\) shown in the figure?

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_10A_Q17_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The equality \(AH=AC=2\) suggests looking for squares. Since \(AC\) consists of two equal pieces of \(AD\), each piece has length \(1\). The corresponding trisection points on the rectangle’s top and bottom sides lie directly above one another. Consequently, \(ACFH\) and \(BDEG\) are both squares of side \(2\).

The figure identifies \(X\) as the intersection of the first square’s diagonals \(AF\) and \(HC\), and \(Z\) as the intersection of the second square’s diagonals \(BE\) and \(DG\). A square’s diagonals meet halfway across and halfway up the square. Thus \(X\) lies directly above \(B\), and \(Z\) lies directly above \(C\), both at height \(1\). Therefore \(XZ\) is horizontal and \(XZ=BC=1\).

A square’s diagonals bisect its right angles. Hence both base angles of \(\triangle WXZ\) are \(45^\circ\), as are both base angles of \(\triangle YXZ\). In either triangle, the perpendicular altitude bisects the base into lengths \(1/2\). The resulting right triangles have two \(45^\circ\) angles, so their legs are equal. Thus each altitude also has length \(1/2\).

Splitting the quadrilateral along \(XZ\) now gives
\[
\text{Area of }WXYZ
=2\left(\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac12\right)
=\frac12.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\tfrac12}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Square centers and triangle areas

solutions.explanation:
Coordinates make the equal spacing and the intersections easy to calculate. Since \(AC=2\) spans two of the three equal pieces of \(AD\), each piece has length \(1\). Place the rectangle at
\[
A=(0,0),\quad D=(3,0),
\]
\[
H=(0,2),\quad E=(3,2).
\]
Its trisection points are
\[
B=(1,0),\quad C=(2,0),
\]
\[
G=(1,2),\quad F=(2,2).
\]
The four lines forming the quadrilateral therefore have equations
\[
AF:\ y=x,\qquad HC:\ y=2-x,
\]
\[
GD:\ y=3-x,\qquad BE:\ y=x-1.
\]
For example, \(W=AF\cap GD\), so \(x=3-x\), giving \(W=(3/2,3/2)\). Solving the other pairs shown in the figure gives
\[
X=(1,1),\qquad Y=(3/2,1/2),
\]
\[
Z=(2,1).
\]
Thus \(XZ\) is a horizontal segment of length \(1\). The perpendicular distances from \(W\) and \(Y\) to its line \(y=1\) are each \(1/2\). Adding the areas of the two triangles on opposite sides of \(XZ\),
\[
\text{Area of }WXYZ
=\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac12
+\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac12
=\frac12.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\tfrac12}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Coordinates and intersections
